description: Hard boundaries. They always apply, are inherited through actor resolution, and are never relaxed by roles, workflows, modes, templates, prompts, or output contracts. Crossing one resolves to status.blocked.

entries.rule: Before any local edit, commit, push, or PR creation: verify current branch, worktree state, HEAD, expected branch scope, and unrelated dirty or untracked files using real git output.
entries.notes: Stop if branch state is unsafe, unrelated work is present, or branch scope is unclear.

entries.rule: main is only a clean pre-branch baseline. Create or switch to the scoped work branch before the first file edit. Uncommitted edits found on main are a recovery state: stop and return the safe status or ask exact PM approval for the recovery action.
Browser chat surfaces never edit files or mutate git/GitHub. PM authorization for writes routes the work to a terminal surface; it never expands browser capability.

Merge, issue closure, labels, tags, releases, settings changes, automation, and target-project artifacts each require separate exact PM approval naming the repository, the issue or PR, and the action. Issue scope, execution mode, or prior approvals never imply them.
Issues close only after review of the real diff, changed files, validation evidence, and risks. Closure produces a closure comment per the traceability protocol before or at closing time.

Durable repository files (kernel, docs, adapters, templates) never store live state: issue/PR/branch/commit/review/validation state, SHAs, GitHub URLs to mutable objects, release readiness, or planning state. Live state lives only in GitHub and git, read at task time.
entries.notes: This is the portability guarantee: any agent reconstructs state from GitHub, never from a stale file or another model's memory.

entries.rule: Never invent git output, repository state, issue state, PR state, validation results, review results, or PM approval. If state is needed and unread, read it live or return status.needs_context.

Never expose or store secrets, credentials, tokens, private keys, sensitive user data, hidden environment values, or confidential operational details, in any file, output, log, command, issue, PR, or comment.

On ambiguous authority, missing kernel files, missing evidence, source conflicts, failed validation, or missing PM approval: stop and return the appropriate non-resolved status. Never guess and proceed.
Output contracts, templates, roles, variables, routing packets, and 'continue' language define shape only. They never grant write permission or authorization.

Code clarity: prefer self-documenting code. When creating or editing code, add concise comments or docstrings for non-obvious intent, domain invariants, state transitions, security-sensitive behavior, external API assumptions, migrations, constraints, and tradeoffs. Do not comment obvious syntax or restate what the code already says.

PM-facing command bundles: use exact repository/issue/PR/branch targets; prefer visible preflight commands; keep scope, risk, and rollback outside executable blocks; no placeholder values when a prior command can provide the concrete value; phase bundles when later commands depend on earlier output; use body files with quoted heredoc delimiters for long GitHub bodies; no 'set -euo pipefail' in PM-facing bundles; never nest triple-backtick fences — when fenced content must carry Markdown that itself contains a fenced block, use a tilde-fenced outer block or move the inner content to a body file; pick a heredoc delimiter that cannot appear in the body.
entries.notes: GitHub CLI --json field safety: only use fields the gh command actually supports. Never use unsupported pseudo-fields such as stateReason or merged in generated validation commands; prefer verified supported fields such as state, closedAt, mergedAt, mergeStateStatus, headRefName, and headRefOid when available. When uncertain, discover supported fields first (e.g. pass an invalid --json value to list them) before producing the bundle.
